description:
User request: separate durable WhatsApp pairing credentials from frequently updated messaging session state, considering ETS or Mnesia. Pending user answer: must session state survive server restart? Do not choose volatile semantics implicitly.

Module-context investigation:
A. Mental model: Amarula owns protocol state; LinkedDevice.Storage translates scoped callbacks to Engine credential_document. Current backend locks connector/credential and decrypts/re-encrypts the entire org grant document for every changed record.
B. Responsibility: Channels owns adapter/runtime; Engine Connect owns encrypted credential storage and authorization; Amarula owns credential and Signal record semantics.
C. Dependencies: Storage -> confidential NodeRouter Event -> CredentialDocuments -> Connect/Repo/encryption. Session onboarding -> TemporaryStorage freeze -> confirm_linked_device -> LinkedDeviceConfirmation transaction -> normal runtime.
D. Contract: synchronous get/put/delete/clear/list_keys/list_profiles; profile and credential binding validation; distinguish miss from unreadable state; guarded adapter stops protocol progress on storage failure.
E. State: creds/self contains pairing identity, keys and mutable one-time prekeys. session contains per-address Signal ratchets; sender_key contains group ratchets. Other namespaces: lid_mapping, device_list, tctoken, app_state_sync_key, app_state_version. These require individual retention decisions; do not treat all non-creds records as disposable.
F. Traces: messaging -> Amarula.SessionStore.store_session -> Storage.put -> Engine document rewrite. Confirmation currently saves ALL frozen provisional records transactionally before starting runtime and discarding snapshot.
G. Invariants: profile isolation, encrypted secret persistence, fail closed on writes, revocation/disable enforcement, restart restoration, idempotent confirmation and complete logout cleanup.
H. Risks: volatile ratchet loss breaks decryption/replay continuity; split stores lose one-database confirmation atomicity; cached authorization must not bypass revocation; persistent Mnesia needs disk lifecycle, encryption, deployment/failover ownership and migration. creds is mutable, not saved once.
I. Coverage: storage_test proves callback restoration/revocation/failure guard; restart_test restores two accounts; confirmation_test covers response-loss idempotence and rollback; credential_documents_concurrency_test covers revoke/disable races and rollback.
J. Unknowns: requested restart durability; deployed volume/node replacement expectations; precise Mnesia durability mode; migration/cutover strategy.

Concrete proposed boundary: keep pairing creds in existing encrypted system credential; route messaging state to a separate profile-scoped store. Recommend persistent encrypted messaging state if continuity is required; ETS-only is a deliberate loss-of-state behavior change. No application code changed.

Action reuse assessment: extend existing LinkedDevice.Storage callbacks and existing confirm_linked_device/credential_document operations, not a parallel pairing or credential framework. Runtime session storage is local protocol infrastructure, not an agent tool. Preserve confidential event boundaries and existing current-binding/revocation contract. Before implementation, define one owner per state class and plan confirmation handoff, migration, revocation and cleanup. Tests must prove session writes do not update canonical credential grants, creds updates still persist, restart behavior matches chosen policy, independent profiles, failures and concurrent cleanup. No UI change or new E2E flow expected.

Policy: docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md Phase 2 requires architectural decision approval; current docs/services/channels.md and prior approved zaq-0l7.2 require durable protocol state and no container file dependency. User authorizes separating storage; exact new durability/deployment contract is pending. Read docs/testing-approach.md and docs/documentation.md before implementation/document edits.

comments.text: Decision approved 2026-10-13: user requests Mnesia RAM, explicitly not disk. Architecture decision resolved; implement session/sender_key RAM only with other protocol credentials durable. Plan tracked in dependent children.

Completed user-approved RAM-only Mnesia split. session/sender_key records use bounded node-local ram_copies with no disk schema/fallback. Pairing and supporting protocol records remain encrypted in canonical credentials. Preserved binding validation; idempotent onboarding seed prevents rollback/resurrection; legacy session namespaces removed on enabled startup. Full precommit passed with 10708 tests and zero failures. Changes remain uncommitted for human review.

title: [zaq-0l7.13] Define WhatsApp pairing and session storage separation
